choices.why: A white three-seat sofa with light birch legs, the most Nordic option, and it fits along the long left wall.
A green wingback armchair on light wooden legs: comfortable for reading and it brings the green you asked for.
A square coffee table in light ash with slim legs, warm and Nordic, sized right between the sofa and the armchair.
A plain beige 200x300 flatweave that holds the whole seating area and softens the wood floor in a cream tone.
A 140 cm table in light ash from the same line as the coffee table, the only one that seats six.
Natural beech chairs with cream paper-cord seats, matching the light wood of the table.
A woven bamboo pendant that gives warmth and texture over the dining table.
A swing-arm floor lamp with a white shade, useful for reading beside the armchair.
A white sideboard with light herringbone wood fronts that keeps the room light and warm.
White linen curtains that filter the light from the window without weighing the room down.
Green linen cushions that tie the white sofa to the green armchair.
A cream cable-knit throw, cozy and in the palette you asked for.
A large areca palm that adds height and green to the corner between the living and dining areas.
A pair of black-and-white abstract prints, minimal and Nordic, side by side above the sofa.
Matte stoneware vases in cream and sage that echo the palette.

answer.why: Light ash and beech woods, cream and white textiles, and touches of green in the armchair, cushions and plants give a warm, cohesive Nordic look against the white walls and oak floor. The bamboo pendant and linen curtains add natural texture.
